objective: Test whether a small set of useful, firsthand Postiz guides can generate verified affiliate referrals and received commission without displacing the primary Local Knowledge Terminal offer or encouraging bulk promotion.

source_evidence.public_reward_claim: Earn 30% per sale for the customer's lifetime.
evidence_boundaries: The Postiz application was accepted on 2026-09-10, and the authenticated dashboard issued one referral link. Acceptance and an issued link do not prove a customer, payout eligibility, or income.
Do not restate the reward as guaranteed monthly income or as forever for the affiliate. The public wording is tied to each customer's lifetime and program terms may change.
Do not claim a fixed seven-day trial. That detail is not stated on the current public program page and must be verified in the accepted program dashboard before use.

The authenticated overview states a 30-day holding period. It does not state the attribution window, eligible-plan boundary, payout threshold, or program-specific reversal rules, so public placement remains paused.
Dub says commission is payable only after the client has paid Dub, a valid payout method and identity verification may be required, and pending or processed dashboard amounts are not cash received.
The issued URL was opened once and resolved to the official Postiz site with Dub attribution parameters. The resulting single dashboard click is a private destination test, not audience interest.

The verified partner business name and user-authorized US checking-account route passed the visible payout precheck. Stripe Connect then presented a human anti-bot challenge. It was not bypassed, and payout remains incomplete.

hypothesis.statement: A real Postiz user can help open-source maintainers, solo builders, and small teams choose and operate a review-first scheduler; if a clearly disclosed referral link appears only after that useful material, some qualified readers may subscribe without reducing trust.
primary_audience: open-source maintainers publishing to two or more social platforms
solo builders who need a reviewable calendar instead of automatic engagement
small teams comparing Postiz cloud service with self-hosting
explicit_needs: schedule different copy and media safely across X, Instagram, and Reddit
connect an agent through the official CLI, API, or MCP without exposing credentials
understand provider-specific media, settings, analytics, and release-verification pitfalls
decide whether managed Postiz or the open-source repository is the better operational fit
not_a_fit: a community that forbids affiliate links or self-promotion
a reader who needs only one platform and no scheduling workflow
any claim based only on a commission percentage rather than a demonstrated Postiz use case

published_assets.title: Postiz CLI and MCP: A Review-First Social Scheduling Workflow
published_assets.verification: Public page returned HTTP 200; the exact title, primary sources, commercial boundary, and translation records were verified.

assets: A reproducible review-first Postiz CLI and MCP setup guide using only official documentation and the operator's verified workflow.
A provider-pitfall checklist covering media upload, live settings discovery, drafts, public release verification, and analytics boundaries.
A candid managed-versus-self-hosted decision guide grounded in the official Postiz repository, including who should not pay for the managed service.
editorial_policy: The standalone answer comes before the referral link.
State firsthand observations narrowly and keep screenshots, dates, and public evidence reviewable.
Include real limitations and a free or self-hosted path where it fits.
Do not use copied praise, invented testimonials, earnings projections, urgency, repeated unsolicited replies, or direct messages.
Create channel-specific drafts and require visible human review before scheduling or publishing.

disclosures.blog: Affiliate disclosure: I use Postiz and may earn a commission if you subscribe through this link. The guide and its limitations come first.
disclosures.short_social: Ad/affiliate: I use Postiz and may earn a commission if you subscribe through this link.
disclosures.video_audio_and_visual: Affiliate disclosure: I may earn a commission if you subscribe through my Postiz link.
disclosures.placement_policy: Put the disclosure with the recommendation and before or next to the link, above any collapsed text. Do not rely on a profile disclosure, an ambiguous 'affiliate link' label, a hashtag cluster, or a platform disclosure control alone.

sequence: Dub-reported signup or trial if that exact event exists
commission received in the connected payout account
funnel.attribution_policy: Use only the exact referral URL issued by Dub. Add channel parameters or aliases only when the accepted program contract or dashboard explicitly supports them. Never place a referral URL in public source code, tests, or a community reply merely to improve attribution.
funnel.truth_policy: Clicks, signups, trials, paid referrals, pending commission, and received commission are distinct. Only received commission enters confirmed gross revenue; a later reversal reduces net revenue.

private_tracking.aggregate_import: Use signals.py only for dated aggregate clicks and signup/trial counts copied from the authenticated Dub dashboard, with evidence under .local/evidence/.
private_tracking.referral_outcome: Record affiliate_referral_confirmed with the campaign ID and a private Dub conversion reference; only its SHA-256 hash is retained.
private_tracking.money_outcomes: Record affiliate_commission_received only after payout receipt is verified. Record affiliate_commission_reversed for a verified clawback or reversal.
private_tracking.privacy: Do not store referred customer names, emails, subscription details, bank data, payout credentials, raw dashboard exports, or referral identifiers in Git.

zero_baseline_2026_09_01.interpretation: These zeroes describe an experiment that has not started; they are not authenticated Dub analytics.

current_checkpoint_2026_09_02.interpretation: The owned tutorial is a verified publication milestone, not authenticated affiliate analytics or revenue. Its links remain untracked until every activation gate passes.

current_checkpoint_2026_09_10.interpretation: The application, issued link, and destination are verified. The only click is the operator's non-purchasing test. Public placement remains paused until payout and placement gates pass; revenue remains zero.

activation_gate: LazyingArt has one Dub partner account and the Postiz application is accepted.
The accepted dashboard and controlling terms have been reviewed; any missing program-specific attribution, payout, reversal, or trial wording is resolved before it is used publicly.
A valid payout method and any required business or identity verification are complete.
The exact Dub-issued referral URL resolves to Postiz and a private test confirms attribution without making a purchase.
Every asset has a clear disclosure, a useful standalone result, and a dated evidence package.
acceptance_criteria.continue_after_one_cycle: Continue for one more capped cycle if there is at least one confirmed paid referral, or at least 25 verified outbound clicks and one dashboard-reported signup or trial. Treat this as experiment evidence, not a revenue forecast.
acceptance_criteria.success: The experiment proves an income channel only after at least one affiliate_commission_received outcome is verified. A paid referral or pending commission alone is not income.

stop_criteria: Do not activate while the payout route is incomplete, required program-specific terms remain unresolved, or the terms conflict with clear disclosure and useful-first content.

Pause immediately if a disclosure is hidden or truncated, a destination changes, a program term changes materially, a platform rule disallows the placement, or a reader reports deceptive or spam-like promotion.
Stop distribution after three useful assets and 30 days if there are fewer than 25 verified outbound clicks; improve the underlying content or audience evidence before another test.
Stop the offer-audience route after 50 verified outbound clicks with zero dashboard-reported signups or trials.
Deprioritize the experiment after two capped cycles and at least 100 verified outbound clicks with zero confirmed paid referrals.
Remove or replace the referral destination if it no longer resolves to the reviewed Postiz offer.

lazyblog.policy: Best primary channel: publish complete searchable tutorials with the disclosure beside the eventual referral link and preserve a non-affiliate official URL for readers who prefer it.

x.policy: First-party account only. Summarize one useful finding, disclose the affiliate relationship in visible copy, and link to the full guide rather than repeating a bare referral link.

instagram.policy: First-party account only. Put the disclosure before collapsed caption text and in both audio and visual form for video; do not publish until the exact provider preview is reviewed.

reddit.policy: Do not place the affiliate link in generated or individualized community replies. A genuinely relevant owned-profile guide may link to the disclosed LazyBlog article after current Reddit rules and the exact public rendering are checked.

hackernews.policy: Hacker News prohibits generated or AI-edited comments. Use needs as product research only and do not publish agent-authored affiliate promotion.

github.policy: Do not add referral links across unrelated repositories. A relevant Postiz integration guide may include one disclosed referral link only after activation and maintainer review.
